title: KiteLoop Renewal & EU On-Prem Roadmap Sync
summary: Quarterly renewal check-in focused on KiteLoop's upcoming renewal window, discussion of capacity reallocation, EU on-prem pilot timeline, security/compliance checklist, and pricing scenarios. Redwood proposes a tiered commitment with burst capacity and an EU on-prem pilot for data residency. Next steps: send updated pricing scenarios, security packet, and schedule a 2-hour technical workshop for on-prem feasibility.
topics: EU on-prem pilot scope and timeline
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-04-09 16:00 UTC
Duration: 38 minutes
Attendees: Samir (Redwood AE), Elena (Redwood SE), Aisha (CTO, KiteLoop), Tom (Head of Platform), Lena (SRE), Ben (Procurement)

[00:00] Samir (Redwood): hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick check, audio ok?
[00:06] Aisha (KiteLoop): yeah, looks good. thanks Samir.
[00:09] Samir: great. so agenda — do a short renewal review, capacity ask, then dive into the eu on-prem pilot timeline. elena will cover technical details after i walk through contract options.
[00:20] Tom (KiteLoop): sounds good, we're especially keen on the eu on-prem piece because of data residency rules for our customers in eu and latency for some eu-edge users.
[00:31] Elena (Redwood): yep, we'll show the proposed architecture and what changes for dedicated vs private. quick note — some transcribed names may be off, sorry in advance if acronyms get mangled.
[00:40] Samir: first, renewal. your term comes up in late may. current committed throughput is 120k tokens/minute reserved across hosted+dedicated pools. you indicated wanting a 30% baseline uplift plus burst. correct?
[00:55] Aisha: right, baseline needs to handle our PLF nightly jobs; bursts are for peak web traffic. we've seen 3x spikes occasionally.
[01:05] Tom: also we want a path to shift some traffic to an eu on-prem cluster for PII processing. initially maybe a small subset — 10-15% of calls — to validate throughput and latency.
[01:19] Elena: makes sense. on the runtime side, for on-prem we'd bring a private control plane with your networking and KMS integration; runtime will be identical but kernel selection changes slightly due to different GPU types.
[01:33] Lena: quick question — if we do on-prem pilot, what's the fallback? i.e., what happens if the cluster misses an SLA or we need more capacity?
[01:40] Samir: good call. we recommend an automated fallback policy to our hosted region or dedicated pool in eu-west; it can route by latency or by policy. there is some added egress time but failsafe keeps traffic flowing.
[01:52] Ben (Procurement): on commercial side, can you outline pricing scenarios? committed vs metered? we want to see the delta, especially for hybrid.
[02:01] Samir: sure. elena and i will follow up with three scenarios: 1) baseline + burst (hosted focused), 2) baseline uplift + reserved dedicated for eu, 3) hybrid with a reserved on-prem pilot plus hosted fallback. we'll include token rates and a monthly committed minimum.
[02:15] Aisha: also our security team will need SOC2 + encryption at rest with our KMS. is that standard for private?
[02:23] Elena: yes, private supports customer-managed KMS/HSM and full audit logs. we also have SSO/SAML and can provide the security pack. small caveat: some hardware attestation steps vary on-prem.
[02:35] Tom: timeline question — how long to stand up a pilot cluster in eu? we're looking at a six week target ideally.
[02:43] Elena: realistically, if infra is provisioned on your side and there's networking peering ready, we can ship an installer and be live in 3-5 weeks for a minimal pilot. full integration with KMS and compliance checks might push to 6-8 weeks.
[02:57] Aisha: who's typically responsible for the installer run? our infra or yours?
[03:02] Samir: it's collaborative. our deployment engineers assist; you own final infra and security approvals.
[03:07] Lena: what about version pinning and rollbacks? we need strict control internally.
[03:11] Elena: you can pin model versions and runtime; rollouts support canary A/B and automatic fallback if quality/regressions detected. that's identical across hosted/dedicated/private.
[03:24] Samir: ok, let's go deeper on capacity math. you currently have 120k tokens/min committed. you said a 30% uplift baseline, that's ~156k tokens/min. if we add a 2x burst headroom, peak could be 312k tokens/min. does that match your telemetry?
[03:42] Tom: yes, that's within the ballpark. some of our late-job batches are token heavy. the main concern is tail latency; we need p95 under 200ms for web lookups.
[03:53] Elena: p95 under 200ms is achievable on eu-dedicated pools with optimized kernels; on-prem depends on GPU type and network fabric — if you pick nvlink capable boxes, that helps.
[04:06] Aisha: noted. Ben: procurement will want a guaranteed SLA for latency or credits. is that negotiable for pilot?
[04:14] Ben: also, can we see references from similarly regulated clients who did the eu pilot?
[04:19] Samir: we can share anonymized case notes and a reference call list. we'll include that in the security packet.
[04:26] [pause / cross talk]
[04:35] Tom: what about data retention on hosted? our compliance team is strict about retention windows and logs.
[04:40] Elena: in hosted, we can set retention policies and provide token-level audit logs; for regulated flows we'd recommend routing to private so logs and data never leave your VPC.
[04:52] Samir: quick objection we get — cost. customers often say private feels expensive upfront. the tradeoff is control and potential savings at scale; our Optimize toolkit can recommend quantization and batching profiles to reduce per-token cost substantially on on-prem.
[05:07] Aisha: anything we should be cautious of technically during pilot?
[05:11] Elena: watch for sequence length distribution changes; if your debug jobs spike sequence lengths, it can throw off batching assumptions. we'll instrument and add guards.
[05:21] Samir: i'd like to propose a commitment structure. option A: 12-month renewal with 30% uplift baseline and metered burst. option B: 12-month with higher committed reserved for eu dedicated and a shorter pilot window. option C: 24-month with on-prem pilot committed capacity and discounted token rate. we'll send detailed dollar numbers.
[05:42] Ben: what are exit terms? we want flexibility if the on-prem pilot doesn't meet latency or compliance needs.
[05:48] Samir: standard is a 60-day notice after the pilot; we can include a pilot clause with an opt-out if KPIs not met. we'll draft that for legal review.
[05:57] Aisha: ok, on technical next steps, we need a 2-hour workshop. can you bring a deployment engineer and someone to walk through KMS and peering requirements?
[06:06] Elena: yes, elena (SE) can lead and our deploy engineer (marvin) will attend. we'll also bring a checklist doc.
[06:15] Tom: scheduling — aim for next wed or thursday?
[06:18] Samir: next wed (2025-04-16) at 14:00 UTC work?
[06:21] Tom: works for us.
[06:23] Aisha: works.
[06:25] [10 minutes of technical detail removed for brevity — notes referenced in follow-up pack]
[16:45] Elena: quick deep dive notes: for on-prem you'll want to expose internal gRPC ports and set up an internal NLB. KV cache persists in local SSD; shared cache requires a redis-like front if you want cross-cluster cache.
[17:00] Lena: local SSD — what's the recovery model on node failures?
[17:03] Elena: auto-rebuild with warmed cache from prefix caching on restart; there is a short warm-up period. we recommend a small warm replica set if you need near-zero cold-start tail latency.
[17:14] Tom: what's monitoring look like? we need token-level cost breakdown and route-level latency.
[17:20] Samir: Redwood Console exposes token-level costing, per-model latencies, and trace hooks. on private we ship a prometheus exporter and also push custom metrics to your ingestion if needed.
[17:32] Ben: procurement asks — can invoicing be consolidated across regions? we prefer a single monthly invoice.
[17:37] Samir: yes, we can consolidate billing, show per-region breakdown line items.
[17:42] Aisha: any blockers you foresee?
[17:44] Elena: mainly infra readiness on KiteLoop side — peering, KMS access, and approved hardware list. once those are in place, it's straightforward.
[17:53] Samir: ok wrapping up, let's confirm next steps and action owners.
[18:00] [end of transcript]
